meta.title: Mia's Water Diagram
meta.textType: functional: a diagram with labels, a blog post

paragraphs: Posted by Mia. On Monday, December fourteenth, I drew a diagram at Lily's kitchen table. It is called "From River to Sink." In science, we learned how water comes to our homes. A diagram is a picture with labels and arrows. My diagram has seven labels: river, electric pump, water tank, pipes, tap, sink, and bathtub. Lily watched me, and she checked each label. Teacher Kim will read my post first.

In step one, the water is in the river. In step two, an electric pump pushes the water into big pipes. The pump needs electricity. It is an important machine. In step three, the pipes carry the water to a tank. Sand in the tank takes the mud out, like in our science experiment. Then it is filtered water. Filtered water is clean. In step four, more pipes bring the clean water to the tap. The water also goes to the sink and the bathtub. Can you see the four numbers on the arrows?

At Lily's house, the tap fills the sink with water. After a snack, Lily and I wash up our cups in a small bowl. In the bathroom, the water fills the bathtub. Used water goes down a pipe under the sink. My mom is a doctor, and she says, "Boiled water is safe to drink." Pip drinks from his own bowl on the kitchen floor. His water is clean, because Lily fills the bowl from the tap.

Lily asked, "Where does the water go after the sink?" I pointed to the last arrow at the end of my diagram. Used water goes to a big center. Engineers clean it there with special equipment. Then the clean water goes back to the river. "The technology is simple, but it is clever," said Lily. Engineers build the pumps, the pipes, and the tanks. I think that engineers have an important job.

Clean water and clean air are important for the environment. Plastic bottles in a river are bad for animals and for people. So please put your plastic bottles in the bin. My idea is to use a bowl, because a bowl saves water. If you turn off the tap, you will save a lot of water. How do you save water at home? Please write to us.
text.summary: Mia posts a diagram called "From River to Sink". It shows the way of water in four steps, from the river and the pump to the tap, and Mia gives a tip to save water.
